heading: Syntax and API guide
intro: These are the less-obvious language or framework features used in this example.

dataclass.title: @dataclass
dataclass.body: The decorator generates methods such as __init__ from annotated class fields; frozen=True prevents field reassignment.

decorators.title: Decorator syntax: @...
decorators.body: A decorator receives the function or class defined immediately below it and returns the object that Python binds to that name.

context-manager.title: The with statement
context-manager.body: A context manager performs setup on entry and guaranteed cleanup on exit, including when the block raises an exception.

class-protocol.title: Double-underscore methods
class-protocol.body: Methods such as __init__, __len__, and __getitem__ connect a class to Python protocols used by construction, len(), indexing, and DataLoader.

comprehensions.title: Comprehension syntax
comprehensions.body: A comprehension builds a collection from an iterable in one expression; read it as the output expression followed by its for and optional if clauses.

unpacking.title: Starred unpacking: * and **
unpacking.body: A single star expands positional items; a double star expands key-value pairs. The same syntax can collect arguments in a function signature.

conditional-expression.title: Inline if/else expression
conditional-expression.body: Python evaluates value_if_true if the condition holds; otherwise it evaluates value_if_false. Unlike an if statement, the expression produces a value.

matrix-multiply.title: Matrix multiplication with @
matrix-multiply.body: For tensors, the @ operator dispatches to matrix multiplication. Its inner dimensions must agree, while leading dimensions may broadcast.

tensor-indexing.title: Tensor slicing and indexing
tensor-indexing.body: Colons select ranges, omitted bounds mean the full available range, and an ellipsis stands for as many untouched dimensions as needed.

tensor-shapes.title: View and shape operations
tensor-shapes.body: reshape, view, flatten, permute, and related methods change how tensor dimensions are interpreted; some return views that share storage.

broadcasting.title: Broadcasting
broadcasting.body: PyTorch aligns dimensions from the right and virtually expands compatible size-1 dimensions without copying their values.

autograd.title: Autograd and backward()
autograd.body: requires_grad asks PyTorch to record differentiable operations. backward() traverses that graph and accumulates derivatives into leaf .grad fields.

inference-mode.title: inference_mode() / no_grad()
inference-mode.body: These contexts disable gradient recording for evaluation. inference_mode adds stronger restrictions and can remove more autograd overhead.

state-dict.title: state_dict checkpoints
state-dict.body: A state dictionary maps registered parameter and buffer names to tensors. Recreate the architecture, then load matching keys into it.

dataset-loader.title: Dataset and DataLoader protocols
dataset-loader.body: Dataset defines how samples are indexed; DataLoader batches those samples and can delegate fetching to worker processes.

model-zoo.title: TorchVision model discovery
model-zoo.body: list_models enumerates registered builders, get_model_weights returns the matching weight enum, and get_model constructs a model by registry name.

image-io.title: decode_image()
image-io.body: TorchVision image I/O decodes encoded bytes into a channel-first tensor. mode="RGB" makes the channel contract explicit before transforms run.

transforms.title: TorchVision transforms v2
transforms.body: A composed transform applies each operation in order. Image conversion, dtype scaling, augmentation, and normalization have distinct roles.

amp.title: Automatic mixed precision
amp.body: autocast chooses lower precision for eligible operations, while GradScaler protects small float16 gradients from underflow during training.

compile.title: torch.compile()
compile.body: torch.compile wraps a callable and specializes captured tensor operations. The first calls may compile, so compare correctness before timing warmed-up runs.

distributed.title: Distributed process APIs
distributed.body: Distributed training runs one Python process per rank. Collectives coordinate tensors, while DDP synchronizes parameter gradients across ranks.

attention.title: Scaled dot-product attention
attention.body: Attention compares queries with keys, scales and normalizes the scores, then uses them to blend values. Mask and dropout arguments change that contract.

convolution.title: Convolution layers
convolution.body: Conv layers learn local kernels. Channel counts, kernel size, stride, padding, and dilation determine the output tensor shape.

loss-functions.title: Loss functions and logits
loss-functions.body: A loss reduces prediction error to a scalar used by backward(). Classification losses usually expect raw logits, not already-normalized probabilities.

optimizer.title: Optimizer step order
optimizer.body: Clear old gradients, compute a fresh loss, call backward(), then call step(). The optimizer updates parameters but does not compute gradients itself.

module.title: nn.Module and forward()
module.body: Subclassing nn.Module registers assigned layers and parameters. Calling model(inputs) invokes framework hooks and then dispatches to forward().

device-placement.title: Tensor and module placement
device-placement.body: to(device) returns a tensor on the requested backend, while Module.to moves registered parameters and buffers in place. Operands must share a device.

randomness.title: Random generators and seeds
randomness.body: A seed initializes a pseudorandom sequence. A dedicated Generator isolates that sequence and must match the device used by the random operation.

export.title: Exported graph boundaries
export.body: Export records a tensor computation graph under stated input assumptions. Python-side effects and unsupported dynamic behavior do not automatically become graph operations.

quantization.title: Weight quantization
quantization.body: Quantization stores or computes selected values at lower precision. Always compare the transformed model with the evaluated floating-point baseline.

profiler.title: Profiler schedules and scopes
profiler.body: The profiler records selected execution windows. Named scopes group lower-level operations so traces can be interpreted at the model-step level.

type-hints.title: Python type annotations
type-hints.body: Annotations document expected inputs and outputs for readers and static tools. Python does not enforce them at runtime unless another library does so.

python-control-flow.title: Python control flow
python-control-flow.body: for, while, if, and try execute ordinary Python decisions around tensor operations. Their indentation defines exactly which statements belong to each block.

tensor-creation.title: Creating tensors
tensor-creation.body: Tensor factory functions define values, shape, dtype, and device. Make those choices explicit when later operations depend on them.

tv-tensors.title: TorchVision TVTensor types
tv-tensors.body: Image and Mask wrap tensors with semantic type information so a v2 transform can apply image interpolation and mask interpolation correctly to the same sample.

model-modes.title: model.train() and model.eval()
model-modes.body: These methods change module behavior; notably, Dropout and BatchNorm behave differently during training and evaluation. They do not enable or disable gradients.

tensor-numpy.title: Tensor and NumPy interoperability
tensor-numpy.body: from_numpy can share CPU memory with an ndarray, while tensor.numpy() requires a CPU tensor that is safe to expose. Mutations may be visible from both objects.

deepcopy.title: copy.deepcopy()
deepcopy.body: A deep copy recursively creates independent contained objects. It is useful for freezing the current best state instead of retaining references that training will mutate.

pathlib.title: Path objects
pathlib.body: pathlib.Path represents filesystem paths as objects and joins path components with the / operator without hand-building platform-specific strings.

temporary-directory.title: TemporaryDirectory
temporary-directory.body: This context manager creates an isolated temporary directory and removes it when the with block ends, which keeps serialization examples self-cleaning.

json-manifest.title: JSON manifests
json-manifest.body: json.dumps serializes only JSON-compatible primitives, lists, and mappings. Converting experiment metadata to this envelope makes it inspectable and portable.

exceptions.title: Explicit exception guards
exceptions.body: raise stops execution with a specific error when an input contract is violated. This remains active even when Python assertions are disabled.

testing.title: torch.testing assertions
testing.body: assert_close compares tensor values with explicit tolerances and reports useful mismatch diagnostics; it is stronger than visually inspecting printed tensors.

probabilities.title: From logits to decisions
probabilities.body: softmax normalizes scores across classes, sigmoid maps independent logits to 0–1 values, and argmax selects an index. Apply the operation that matches the task contract.

sequence-padding.title: pad_sequence
sequence-padding.body: pad_sequence stacks variable-length tensors after extending shorter sequences with a padding value. The resulting layout depends on batch_first.

torch-cond.title: torch.cond()
torch-cond.body: torch.cond represents tensor-dependent branching inside an exportable graph. Both branch functions must satisfy the documented input and output restrictions.

iterators.title: Iterators and lazy traversal
iterators.body: iter creates a stream of values, next consumes one value, and itertools tools transform or limit a stream without materializing every item first.

comments.trainingMode: Enable training behavior for stateful layers before computing this epoch.
comments.evaluationMode: Use deterministic evaluation behavior for layers such as Dropout and BatchNorm.
comments.clearGradients: Gradients accumulate by default, so clear values left by the previous step.
comments.backwardPass: Differentiate the scalar loss and populate gradients on learnable parameters.
comments.optimizerStep: Update each parameter using the gradients computed above.
comments.inferenceContext: Evaluation does not need an autograd graph, so disable gradient bookkeeping.
comments.autocastContext: Run eligible operations in lower precision inside this scoped context.
comments.saveCheckpoint: Serialize an explicit state envelope rather than the live Python model object.
comments.loadCheckpoint: Load onto CPU first, then validate the envelope before moving tensors to an accelerator.
comments.compileBoundary: Compile only the tensor-heavy callable after establishing an eager reference.
comments.parityCheck: Require the optimized path to agree numerically with the eager reference.
comments.initializeDistributed: Join this process to the distributed group before using collectives.
comments.cleanupDistributed: Release process-group resources even when the worker is finishing.
comments.samplerEpoch: Change the distributed sampler seed each epoch while keeping ranks coordinated.
